usage: Used as a unit noun for weight, usually after a number or quantity word: e.g. 1 公斤, 2.5 公斤. In Cantonese it sounds natural in shopping, cooking, and weighing things.
Common in measure phrases with numerals and classifiers. You can also add approximate words like 大約 or 差唔多 before the quantity.
Very often used for food and body weight, especially when talking about meat, fruit, luggage, or exercise goals.
In everyday Hong Kong speech, 斤 is still very common in wet markets, while 公斤 is the standard metric unit in more formal, school, and written contexts.
